# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95
Labels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api

## Why

The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads "no errors" while the caller sees rejections.

Recorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.

## What to do

Call `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged
- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`
- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass

## Tech notes

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

Out of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).

1	# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks
2	
3	| Field  | Value                |
4	| ------ | -------------------- |
5	| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |
6	| Status | Shipped              |
7	
8	`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.
9	
10	## Installing hooks through config
11	
12	- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).
13	- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).
14	- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).
15	- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).
16	- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).
17	- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).
18	- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).
19	
20	## Engine startup
21	
22	- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).
23	
24	## Measured semantics — out of scope
25	
26	This property of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` is recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue does not change it; that is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.
27	
28	- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks

| Field  | Value                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |
| Status | Shipped              |

`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.

## Installing hooks through config

- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).
- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).
- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).
- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).
- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).
- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).
- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).

## Engine startup

- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).

## Measured semantics — out of scope

This property of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` is recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue does not change it; that is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.

- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

# AGENTS.md

## Context Loading Order

Agents should read files in this order to understand the HAL Engine codebase:

1. **README.md** - Overview, features, quick start, and project structure
2. **package.json** - Dependencies, scripts, tech stack validation
3. **tsconfig.json** - TypeScript configuration and compilation targets
4. **src/index.ts** - Public API exports and module surface
5. **src/config.ts** - Main factory function `createHalEngine()` and configuration schema
6. **src/types/** - Core type definitions (ai.ts, session.ts, messages.ts, auth.ts, sessionStore.ts)
7. **src/providers/** - AI provider implementations (bedrock, vertex, openai, anthropic, mock)
8. **src/infrastructure/** - Support layers (builders, stores, parsers)
9. **src/orchestration/** - Business logic (chatOrchestrator, tools, context management)
10. **src/transport/** - Server setup (Express app, WebSocket, routes)
11. **specs/** - Normative specs (architecture, WebSocket protocol, providers, tool responses)
12. **adrs/** - Architecture Decision Records
13. **docs/** - How-to guides, coding practices, and research spikes under docs/spikes/
14. **.specify/spec.md** - Repo-level system spec (exempt from the spec header table convention)

## Workflow Commands

### Development
```bash
npm run dev          # Start example/server.ts with hot reload (tsx watch)
npm run typecheck    # Run TypeScript type checking without emitting
```

### Building
```bash
npm run build        # Compile TypeScript to dist/ (tsc)
npm start            # Run compiled JavaScript from dist/index.js
```

### Testing
```bash
npm test             # Run Jest test suite
# Tests use ts-jest for TypeScript compilation
# Configuration: jest.config.js
```

### Code Quality
```bash
npm run eslint       # Run ESLint with max-warnings 0 (zero-tolerance)
npm run prettier     # Format all src/**/*.ts with Prettier
npm run prettier:check  # Check formatting without writing
```

### All Checks (Recommended Pre-Commit)
```bash
npm run verify
```

That is the blocking set `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `verify` job runs on every
pull request, in the same order, and `scripts/verify-script.test.ts` fails if the
two stop agreeing - so this command cannot quietly become a subset of what CI
demands. Two gates in that job are missing from it because both diff against
`origin/main` and neither runs the same way on a checkout: the spec anchor check
and the changelog check.

Two further CI jobs are worth running locally before a release or a change that
touches packaging: `npm run check:build-chain` (audit and action pins) and
`npm run smoke` (packs the tarball and installs it outside this tree).

## Spec Header Table

Every `specs/*/spec.md` opens with its title, then a two-column header table,
and carries a lead paragraph of prose before its first `##` section:

```markdown
# <spec title>

| Field  | Value                  |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#<n> |
| Status | Draft                  |

<lead paragraph>
```

# Written for this repo's Jest suite rather than adapted from the Vitest
# equivalent for a Vitest suite: the report shapes happen to match, but the
# invocations do not.
- id: hal-engine-jest
  name: HAL Engine Jest suite
  cwd: .
  description: >-
    The ts-jest unit suite over src/ and scripts/ (jest.config.js roots), run
    on every pull request in .github/workflows/ci.yml as the "Test" step.
    Selectors are "<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>" as emitted by the
    list command. Jest has no dry-run, so the list command executes the suite
    once with --json and derives every name from the report; it deliberately
    tolerates a red suite, since listing must not depend on the tests passing.
    The run command selects one test with --runTestsByPath plus an anchored,
    regex-escaped -t, and treats a selector that matches nothing as a failure
    rather than a green run of an empty suite. Neither command builds first:
    no test here reads dist/.
  list: node scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs
  run: node scripts/lore-run-test.mjs "{selector}"
  coverage_format: lcov

5	  testMatch: ['**/*.test.ts'],
6	  // Fixture suites are inputs to the gate tests, not tests; one of them is deliberately skipped.
7	  testPathIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/', '/scripts/fixtures/'],
8	  extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts'],
9	  moduleFileExtensions: ['ts', 'js', 'json'],
10	  // NodeNext source writes `./x.js` for `./x.ts`; jest resolves the real file.
11	  moduleNameMapper: {

13	  },

15	    '^.+\\.tsx?$': ['ts-jest', {useESM: true}],
16	  },
17	  // src/ only: the scripts/ suites drive their subjects through spawnSync, so an
18	  // instrumented .mjs would report zero regardless of how well it is tested.
19	  collectCoverageFrom: ['src/**/*.ts', '!src/**/*.test.ts', '!src/providers/providerTestSupport.ts', '!src/infrastructure/writeSignalTestSupport.ts', '!src/shared/logCaptureTestSupport.ts', '!src/transport/wsTestSupport.ts', '!src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoTestSupport.ts'],
20	  // A ratchet, not a target: these are exactly what the suite measured when the
21	  // gate landed, so any drop fails and any rise should move them up with it. A
22	  // red run is fixed by adding the missing test, never by lowering the number
23	  // (specs/hal-engine-npm-release/spec.md).
24	  // The one exception: deleting covered code shrinks the denominator and lowers
25	  // the percentage while the uncovered count is unchanged. Compare covered/total
26	  // absolutes before re-baselining, and say so in the commit.
27	  // Per-path floors set at measurement, exactly as the global row is. An earlier version set them at
28	  // 70 with a comment claiming all four sat well above it - vertex's branches were 69.23, below it, and
29	  // four groups gained an 18-to-30 point regression budget the single global floor had never allowed.
30	  // `src/orchestration/tools/` is named separately because a path floor is a prefix match: without it a
31	  // regression in the tools registry hides inside the orchestration figure, which is what these exist
32	  // to prevent. Naming a path REMOVES its files from the `global` group, so the global numbers below
33	  // cover the remainder - the provider adapters and ws helpers with no suite - and are lower for that
34	  // reason rather than because coverage fell. Raise any of these with the measurement; never lower one

1	import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
2	import {dirname, basename, join} from 'node:path';
3	import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
4	import eslint from '@eslint/js';
5	import markdown from '@eslint/markdown';
6	import reLint from '@re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint';
7	import tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';
8	import {parse as parseYaml} from 'yaml';
9	
10	// layers.yaml is the readable declaration of the architecture; this hands it
11	// to no-cross-layer-import.
12	//
13	// The rule keys packages by `<package>/src/`, which suits a monorepo of
14	// packages and not a single package whose code sits at ./src. Left to find
15	// layers.yaml itself the rule would resolve every file as `src/...`, match no
16	// package, and report nothing - adopted in appearance, enforcing nothing. So
17	// the entries are re-homed under this checkout's own directory name with the
18	// root moved one level up, which is the shape the matcher expects.
19	//
20	// Paths come from this file's own URL rather than process.cwd(), so running
21	// eslint from a subdirectory cannot silently disable the rule.
22	// scripts/eslint-layers.test.ts fails if this ever stops reporting.
23	const repoRoot = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
24	const declaredLayers = parseYaml(readFileSync(join(repoRoot, 'layers.yaml'), 'utf8')).layers.src;
25	
26	// Shared with eslint.config.backlog.mjs, which lints the same tree under the
27	// two rules held out of the blocking gate. One list, so the two configs cannot
28	// drift into disagreeing about what is even a source file.
29	//
30	// .claude/** is vendored agent tooling, maintained upstream rather than
31	// here, so a change there must not be able to redden this repo's CI.
32	export const ignores = [
33	  'node_modules/**',
34	  'dist/**',
35	  'coverage/**',
36	  '.claude/**',
37	  // Deliberately broken specs and ADRs - dead links, absent lead paragraphs,
38	  // statuses no parser reads - kept as the fixtures the script tests assert
39	  // against. Linting them would report the very faults they exist to reproduce.
40	  'scripts/fixtures/**',
41	];
42	
43	export default tseslint.config(
44	  {ignores},
45	  {
46	    // Scoped to TypeScript now that markdown is linted too: an unscoped block
47	    // applies to every language, and JS rules do not survive a markdown AST.
48	    files: ['**/*.ts'],
49	    extends: [eslint.configs.recommended, ...tseslint.configs.recommended],
50	    plugins: {'re-lint': reLint},
51	    rules: {
52	      // CLAUDE.md leads with five mandatory layers and "no cross-layer
53	      // shortcuts, no circular deps". layers.yaml states that as data and this
54	      // rule enforces it, so the architecture is a file someone can read rather
55	      // than a habit that erodes.
56	      're-lint/no-cross-layer-import': [
57	        'error',
58	        {root: dirname(repoRoot), layers: {[basename(repoRoot)]: declaredLayers}},
59	      ],
60	      '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars': [
61	        'error',
62	        {
63	          vars: 'all',
64	          args: 'after-used',
65	          argsIgnorePattern: '^_',
66	          varsIgnorePattern: '^_',
67	          caughtErrorsIgnorePattern: '^_',
68	          ignoreRestSiblings: false,
69	        },
70	      ],
71	      camelcase: 'error',
72	      // CLAUDE.md: "Tests live next to source: src/**/*.test.ts". True of all
73	      // ten test files today; this keeps it true.
74	      're-lint/require-colocated-tests': 'error',
75	      're-lint/no-commented-out-code': 'error',
76	      // The provider layer must surface failures as AIError rather than
77	      // swallowing them and fabricating a return value (CLAUDE.md, Adding a
78	      // provider).
79	      're-lint/no-catch-as-control-flow': 'error',
80	      // Markdown is excluded because a doc quoting the code it documents is
81	      // the intended state: README's example of createHalEngine and the
82	      // interface blocks in specs/ are *supposed* to match src/. jscpd extracts
83	      // fenced blocks and reports them as clones, so without this every
84	      // accurate code sample is a lint error and the incentive is to let the
85	      // docs drift. The same exclusion a jscpd config would carry; it lives
86	      // here rather than in a .jscpd.json because the rule reads `ignore` from
87	      // its own options and never from a config file.
88	      're-lint/no-duplicate-code': ['error', {ignore: ['**/*.md']}],
89	      're-lint/callee-below-caller': 'error',
90	      're-lint/declare-near-use': 'error',
91	      're-lint/default-export-matches-filename': 'error',
92	      're-lint/max-boolean-operators': 'error',
93	      're-lint/max-comment-lines': 'error',
94	      're-lint/max-member-chain': 'error',
95	      're-lint/no-closing-brace-comments': 'error',
96	      're-lint/no-flag-params': 'error',
97	      // INERT, kept as a placeholder. It needs type information and this config
98	      // gives it none, so it reports nothing - verified with a textbook
99	      // forwarding class, which it does not flag. The rule's own docs record the
100	      // same finding for the same reason. It becomes a real guardrail only if
101	      // this config adopts parserOptions.projectService; until then it is not
102	      // one, and a clean run says nothing about forwarding classes.
103	      're-lint/no-forwarding-class': 'error',
104	      're-lint/no-hybrid-class': 'error',
105	      're-lint/no-negative-names': 'error',
106	      're-lint/no-nested-if': 'error',
107	      're-lint/no-nested-loop': 'error',
108	      're-lint/no-reexport-only-module': 'error',
109	      're-lint/no-vague-names': 'error',
110	      're-lint/prefer-early-return': 'error',
111	      're-lint/prefer-polymorphism': 'error',
112	      're-lint/require-fetch-timeout': 'error',
113	      'no-console': 'error',
114	      // Providers are loaded lazily so that selecting one never forces its SDK
115	      // on consumers of the others, and the factories doing it are synchronous
116	      // (`createProvider`, `createBedrockProvider`) - dynamic `import()` would
117	      // make them async, which is a breaking API change. The rule stays on and
118	      // still rejects every other `require()`; only these paths are permitted.
119	      '@typescript-eslint/no-require-imports': [
120	        'error',
121	        {allow: ['^\\./(bedrock|vertex|openai|anthropic|mock)/index\\.js$', '^@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime$']},
122	      ],
123	    },
124	  },
125	  // Rules that only make sense on a test file.
126	  {
127	    // require-spec-link gates here: every test in
128	    // the suite cites a spec statement, so the backlog it once measured is
129	    // empty and an uncited new test is now a build failure rather than a
130	    // number. Its statement-side mirror stays a report - see
131	    // eslint.config.backlog.mjs.
132	    files: ['**/*.test.ts'],
133	    plugins: {'re-lint': reLint},
134	    rules: {
135	      're-lint/require-spec-link': 'error',
136	      're-lint/max-expects': 'error',
137	      're-lint/no-nondeterministic-tests': 'error',
138	      're-lint/test-imports-its-subject': 'error',
139	    },
140	  },
141	  // Every markdown link to a repo file must land. A rename sweep rewrites a
142	  // dead link faithfully and the reference still reads as current, which is
143	  // exactly how the spec restructure could have gone wrong.
144	  {
145	    files: ['**/*.md'],
146	    language: 'markdown/gfm',
147	    plugins: {markdown, 're-lint': reLint},
148	    rules: {'re-lint/no-dead-md-links': 'error'},
149	  },
150	  // AGENTS.md § Spec Header Table: every spec and ADR opens with a lead
151	  // paragraph, and a spec's `| Status |` row must match its test-citation
152	  // coverage. ADRs are exempt from the coverage tier - asking a decision
153	  // record to cite a test for every statement it makes is the wrong ask - so
154	  // the second rule is scoped to specs alone.
155	  {
156	    files: ['specs/**/spec.md', 'adrs/*.md', 'scripts/fixtures/spec-status/**/*.md'],
157	    language: 'markdown/gfm',
158	    plugins: {markdown, 're-lint': reLint},
159	    rules: {'re-lint/require-intro-paragraph': 'error'},
160	  },
161	  {
162	    files: ['specs/**/spec.md', 'scripts/fixtures/spec-status/specs/**/spec.md'],
163	    language: 'markdown/gfm',
164	    plugins: {markdown, 're-lint': reLint},
165	    // require-statement-links belongs to this pair but is deliberately absent:
166	    // see eslint.config.backlog.mjs.
167	    rules: {'re-lint/require-status-matches-coverage': 'error'},
168	  }
169	);
